title: Show where an apple goes
premise: An arrow can explain that an apple goes into a basket if it ends inside the opening.
context: A short graphic-placement transfer test with an actual basket part and a controlled composition.
signature: Pocket Cutouts: original plum outlined apple and ochre open basket on ivory paper; no baked text.

cues.say: An apple sits beside a basket.
A precise arrow points into the opening, not at the rim.

apple.visual: ONE simple juicy red apple and a green leaf on clean flat white; object fills the center, no floor shadow

basket.visual: ONE round OPEN ochre wicker basket with a LARGE dark empty oval interior at the top. No arch handle, no lettering, clean flat white background and no floor shadow.

anchors.opening: a point inside the dark empty opening at the top of this one woven basket, away from its light rim

panels.visual: One apple beside one open wicker basket, separated by clean negative space.
panels.keep: Use actual reusable illustrated cutouts, not free-form additional fruit.

panels.visual: Show the apple's destination inside the basket opening.
panels.change: A gold arrow from apple body to the basket opening.
panels.keep: Absolutely identical illustrated cutouts and their positions.
